hypothesis.text: A society organized through dense, voluntary, locally rooted and networked civic institutions may increase participation, trust, accountability, community problem-solving and democratic resilience by giving citizens repeated opportunities to exercise meaningful agency over the institutions affecting their lives.
hypothesis.central_question: Can dense, voluntary, locally rooted and networked civic institutions increase participation, trust, accountability, community problem-solving and democratic resilience without making political rights contingent on participation or enforcing political conformity?
hypothesis.constitutional_capitalism_test: Can Constitutional Capitalism cultivate a culture in which self-government is something citizens do together—through ordinary participation, service, informed disagreement and community stewardship—while preserving universal political rights that never depend on how much a person participates?

governance.reason: Steve-directed opening of a major cultural-layer research track. Architecture remains frozen: register as hypothesis/system for research only; do not mint a principle or doctrine until evidence graduates under falsifiability, including failure modes.

hard_boundary.rule: Participation should be treated as a civic duty, but political rights must never depend on participation.
forbids: You did not participate enough, so you have less voice

cultural_ideal.statement: Self-government is not something government does for citizens. It is something citizens do together.

end_state_contrast.to: Who in our community needs to come together to fix this, and what part am I responsible for?

philosophical_research_statement.text: Liberty creates both rights and responsibilities. A free society cannot remain free if citizens surrender responsibility for governing their communities to political parties, corporations, bureaucracies, wealthy interests or professional political classes. Self-government therefore requires a culture in which participation, service, informed disagreement and community stewardship are ordinary expectations of citizenship.

hard_distinctions.rule: Civic duty expectation ≠ rights conditioned on participation.
hard_distinctions.target: Universal political rights remain intact regardless of participation level.

hard_distinctions.rule: Universal civic expectation ≠ compulsory political conformity.
hard_distinctions.target: Duty is to participate honestly, not to agree.

hard_distinctions.rule: Civic Record ≠ government score or rights qualification.
hard_distinctions.target: Voluntary record of service (hours, projects, organizations, skills, outcomes) — never a franchise or speech gate.

hard_distinctions.rule: Civic connectivity ≠ party registration or ideological affiliation.
hard_distinctions.target: Prosperity/civic indicator = share of population connected to functioning civic relationships.

hard_distinctions.rule: Productive disagreement = civic participation, not civic failure.
hard_distinctions.target: Show up, listen, argue, accept legitimate process, keep working with neighbors.
Some decisions must genuinely move downward or participation becomes irrational.
No new principle under architecture freeze.

hard_distinctions.rule: People's News / local journalism ≠ civic networks alone.
hard_distinctions.target: Information creates visibility; networks create relationships capable of acting on information — two pieces of one system.

architecture.name: Distributed Civic Commons
architecture.basic_unit: Extremely small — small enough that people know one another (neighborhoods, blocks, apartment communities, rural roads, school communities, workplaces, churches, civic organizations).

communication_directions.downward: Government and institutions communicate to citizens
communication_directions.sideways: Communities communicate with one another — required so the system does not become dependent on a central authority

participation_as_normal_life.reject: You should get politically involved once every four years.
participation_as_normal_life.aim: This is simply part of being a member of this community.
participation_as_normal_life.capacity_rule: People contribute according to time, skills, age and capacity.

granularity_measure.not: We have 30,000 residents / party registration / ideological affiliation
granularity_measure.yes: We have N functioning community networks, active precinct groups, neighborhood organizations, school-community networks, and citizens participating in some form
granularity_measure.definition_draft: Share of the population connected to functioning civic relationships
granularity_measure.prosperity_link: Disconnected communities are harder to organize around schools, disasters, economic opportunities, healthcare, elections or development

communication_as_civic_infrastructure.control_rule: No single private company or government platform should control the communication network
communication_as_civic_infrastructure.convergence: People's News / local journalism creates information; civic networks create relationships capable of acting on information

continuous_civic_education.model: Arkansas Civic University-type education that does not end at graduation

What does the quorum court actually do?

How do I run for office?
How do I organize a petition?

meaningful_decisions.problem: Attend a meeting → speak for three minutes → officials ignore you
meaningful_decisions.lesson: My participation can actually change something

track_a_culture_and_practice.title: Cultural norms, prestige systems, and ordinary participation doors under existing law

multi-medium civic information infrastructure without single-controller platforms

track_c_failure_modes.title: Falsification and harm research

journalism.rule: People's News / local journalism and the Distributed Civic Commons are two pieces of the same system.

prosperity.note: Honor and optional recognition only; no franchise dependency.
